Soojin / Dylan —

Read Elaine's note and their redline. High level legal take: 

1) Renewal notice window: 90 days is standard for us on multi-year commitments; 60 days is an acceptable compromise for a strategic customer. 30 days is too short operationally (we need time to re-provision capacity and manage backfills).

2) Termination for convenience: We should avoid an unrestricted termination-for-convenience right in year one. Two reasonable approaches depending on the commercial ask: 
   - Option A (preferred for revenue protection): 12-month minimum term during which termination for convenience is not permitted; after 12 months, either party may terminate with 60 days' notice.
   - Option B (more flexible): Allow termination for convenience with 60 days' notice but include an early-termination charge equal to the remaining prepaid months or a percentage of the committed ARR for the remainder of the initial term.

3) Order Form alignment: The Order Form must mirror whatever we land on in the MSA (term length, renewal cadence, notice window). Ensure there's explicit language that Order Form supersedes any internal reference to different renewal cadence.

Suggested next step: Propose 60-day mutual notice for renewal + Option A for termination (12-month initial lock with 60-day post-12mo termination). If the customer pushes back strongly on Option A, we can fallback to Option B with a clearly defined early-termination fee.

I'll draft sample clause language you can send to Horizon. Suggest we aim to close the redline this week so we can push to signature in the first week of September.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Elaine / Michael —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing Horizon's redline. Per Marissa's guidance we propose the following compromise for the MSA and mirrored in the Order Form: 

1) Renewal notice window: 60 days prior written notice to opt out of auto-renewal (mutual).

2) Termination for convenience: Option A adopted — initial 12-month minimum term during which no termination for convenience is permitted. After the initial 12 months, either party may terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice.

3) If Horizon is unable to accept Option A, Redwood will consider Option B: Horizon may terminate for convenience at any time with 60 days' notice, and an early-termination fee equal to the lesser of (i) the remaining prepaid months or (ii) 25% of the remaining committed ARR for the initial term.

I've attached an updated Order Form redline that aligns the term language and includes the sample clauses (file: Redline_OrderForm_Horizon_20250819.xlsx). Please review with your legal and let us know whether Option A is acceptable or whether we should proceed with Option B.

If Option A is acceptable, we can issue a clean MSA and Order Form for signature and route through DocuSign. If Option B is required, we need agreement on the early-termination fee calculation before we finalize pricing.

Can you let us know by COB Friday (Aug 22) so we can keep the commercial terms in place?

Thanks —
Soojin
